conclusive_probe.method: created a throwaway object under the protected prefix, captured its REAL VersionId, and attempted to delete that version
conclusive_probe.result: AccessDenied — 'User: arn:aws:iam::219024422756:user/admin is not authorized to perform: s3:DeleteObjectVersion ... with an explicit deny in a resource-based policy'
conclusive_probe.significance: the Deny bites for the ADMINISTRATIVE principal, which is the principal that could otherwise remove the artifact. This is the control actually being claimed.

deliberate_orphan.status: PERMANENTLY UNDELETABLE BY DESIGN — its undeletability is the evidence. It is a few dozen bytes and is not to be 'cleaned up'; removing it would require weakening the control it demonstrates.

behavioural_proof.first_two_probes_were_INCONCLUSIVE_and_a: attempts to delete a synthetic version id returned InvalidArgument on the protected prefix, on an unprotected prefix, AND on the long-protected validation/ prefix. S3 format-validates a version id BEFORE authorization, so that probe cannot discriminate and proves nothing. It is recorded rather than discarded, because a probe that returns the same answer everywhere is a probe that would have 'passed' against a policy that did nothing.

mutation_control.conclusion: the Deny is prefix-scoped and effective: denied under runtime-custody/*, permitted under an unprotected prefix.
mutation_control.method: identical object and identical delete under an UNPROTECTED prefix in the SAME bucket
mutation_control.why: a deny proof is worthless if the test would deny everything. The control proves the test discriminates.

behavioural_proof.why: policy text is not behaviour. The program's own lesson, recorded in the Validation-2 custody record: 'proven from the evaluator host itself, not inferred from policy text. This is the check whose absence cost a latch cycle this morning.'
